canonicalIngredients.name: self-raising flour
observations: 150 g plain flour + 1/2 tsp baking powder (s3)

canonicalIngredients.name: oil
observations: 1/2 tsp olive, tin-greasing only, none in batter (s1)

canonicalIngredients.name: butter
observations: 1 tbsp, saute fat for bacon and onion (s2)

canonicalIngredients.name: dried Italian herbs
observations: 1/2 tsp, plus 1/4 tsp chilli flakes, 1/2 tsp onion flakes (s3)

causalSequence: preheat 180C (160C fan); grease, line slab tin (16x26 to 20x30 cm)
grate zucchini; squeeze out excess moisture
stir in zucchini, onion, cheese, flour, oil; season salt pepper
bake 30-45 min until set, golden, firm to touch
techniqueFacts: classic slice carries bacon; vegetarian variant = omit it entirely (3 sources), with cheese + extra veg (corn, carrot, roasted capsicum, sun-dried tomato, sauteed mushroom, feta) covering the savoury gap
squeezing the grated zucchini dry is the anti-sogginess lever (3 sources; s2 salts it in a colander first to draw moisture)
self-raising flour gives the fluffy muffin-like set; sub is 1 cup plain flour + 2 tsp baking powder (s2), s3 builds it from plain flour + baking powder
AU method is one-bowl, everything combined raw; s2 (US) sautes onion (and bacon) in butter first for flavour
done cues: golden top, springs back, skewer near-clean, edges pull from tin; bottom rack helps the base brown (s0)
resting 10-15 min after baking firms the slice for clean cutting (s1, s3)
eats hot or cold; fridge 3-5 days, freezes 2-3 months, freezer-friendly per all sources
keeps a tender moist crumb - firmer than frittata, softer than bread (s0); s3 grills last few minutes for a crisper top
